content: Lamivudine, marketed under the brand name EPIVIR and also known as 3TC, is a synthetic nucleoside analogue with antiviral activity against both HIV-1 and HBV. Its chemical name is (2R, cis)-4-amino-1-(2-hydroxymethyl-1,3-oxathiolan-5-yl)-(1H)-pyrimidin-2-one. Lamivudine is the (-) enantiomer of a dideoxy analogue of cytidine and is also referred to as (-)2′,3′-dideoxy, 3′-thiacytidine. Lamivudine appears as a white to off-white crystalline solid and has a solubility of approximately 70 mg/mL in water at 20°C. EPIVIR is available in tablet form for oral administration. Each scored 150-mg film-coated tablet contains 150 mg of lamivudine along with the following inactive ingredients: hypromellose, magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, polyethylene glycol, polysorbate 80, sodium starch glycolate, and titanium dioxide. The 300-mg film-coated tablet contains 300 mg of lamivudine and the same inactive ingredients, with the addition of black iron oxide. EPIVIR is also available as an oral solution for oral administration. Each milliliter (1 mL) of the oral solution contains 10 mg of lamivudine (10 mg/mL) in an aqueous solution. The inactive ingredients in the oral solution include artificial strawberry and banana flavors, anhydrous citric acid, methylparaben, propylene glycol, propylparaben, sodium citrate dihydrate, and sucrose (200 mg).
